name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM) student scholarship — umbrella rules
funder: European Commission / EACEA (Erasmus+ Key Action 2)
amount_detail: Unit contribution of EUR 1,400/month x DS (duration of the Master in months). Programme Guide formula quoted verbatim: "1 400 Euros/month x DS". For a 24-month EMJM that is EUR 33,600 total; 18 months = EUR 25,200; 12 months = EUR 16,800. NOTE — under the post-2021 EMJM design this single monthly unit REPLACED the old EMJMD three-part split (participation costs / travel+installation / subsistence). The Programme Guide states the amount "shall cover travel, visa, installation and subsistence costs" as one lump. There is NO separately published Partner-Country uplift in the 2021+ EMJM rules — the EUR 1,400/month is the same regardless of nationality. Individual consortia may still publish their own internal breakdown (e.g. EUR 1,275/month subsistence + separate travel/installation), which is a consortium presentation choice, not an EC rule.
covers: No tuition/participation fees for scholarship holders ("projects cannot charge tuition fees or other mandatory costs related to student participation in the course to Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders"); no application fee; plus EUR 1,400/month covering travel, visa, installation and subsistence.
eligibility_verbatim: "EMJM scholarships can be offered to students from all over the world. However, consortia should ensure geographical balance – i.e. no more than 10% of the total number of scholarships awarded during project implementation should be awarded to candidates from the same nationality." Students must be "enrolled at Master level who have obtained a first higher education degree or demonstrate a recognised equivalent level of learning."
exclusion_clause_verbatim: No nationality exclusion found. The only nationality-linked constraint quoted in the Programme Guide is the geographical-balance cap: "no more than 10% of the total number of scholarships awarded during project implementation should be awarded to candidates from the same nationality." (Tunisia is not a high-volume EMJM nationality, so this cap is unlikely to bind.)
deadline_2027_intake: Set per consortium, not centrally. EMJM calls for an autumn intake typically close between October and February of the PRECEDING academic year — i.e. for a September 2027 start, expect deadlines roughly Oct 2026 – Feb 2027. NOT FOUND as a central date; must be checked per programme.
path_codes: A | B | C | AA | AB | AC | X
notes: CRITICAL CORRECTION TO THE WORKING ASSUMPTION: the belief that Partner-Country status INCREASES the EMJM award is true of the OLD Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degrees (EMJMD, 2014-2020 calls), where participation-cost caps were EUR 9,000/yr for Programme Country vs EUR 25,000/yr for Partner Country students and travel/installation was EUR 1,000 vs EUR 3,000. Under the current EMJM design (2021+ calls, which is what a Sept 2027 intake will be) the grant is a flat EUR 1,400/month for everyone. Tunisian status is therefore neutral on the money, not favourable — but it is fully eligible. Second point: Tunisia is a "third country not associated to the Programme" (Region 3, South-Mediterranean). Being in that category is what makes a Tunisian applicant a normal, welcome EMJM candidate rather than one competing inside an EU quota. Third point: a Tunisian applicant with NO prior EU residency is exactly the profile EMJM targets; the only residency-linked rule some consortia apply is a mobility rule (you cannot do your mobility in the country where you obtained your first degree) — irrelevant here.

Third: consortium is Universidad de Murcia (Spain) + Lund University (Sweden) + Friedrich-Alexander-Universitaet Erlangen-Nuernberg (Germany). amount_detail: Means-tested and componentised. covers: Tuition (precios públicos) plus income- and residence-linked cash components for official university study including máster universitario.

For EU nationals: 'tú o tu familia tenéis que residir de forma permanente en España o acreditar un trabajo por cuenta propia o ajena en España' (otherwise only the tuition component). For non-EU nationals: 'puedes tener derecho a beca si eres menor de 18 años o si has obtenido permiso de residencia a 31 de diciembre de 2025.' Also general: 'No haber obtenido un título de nivel igual o superior a los estudios para los que pides la beca.' Master-specific: first year requires enrolment in 'mínimo 60 créditos' (30 with limitations) and 'nota media de 5 puntos en los estudios que dan acceso al máster'.
exclusion_clause_verbatim: 'No es suficiente tener concedida la autorización de estancia.' (becaseducacion.gob.es, requisitos generales, non-EU applicants — immediately following 'puedes tener derecho a beca si eres menor de 18 años o si has obtenido permiso de residencia a 31 de diciembre de 2025.') THIS IS THE DECISIVE CLAUSE. A Tunisian student entering Spain on a study visa holds an 'autorización de estancia por estudios', not a 'permiso de residencia' — expressly declared insufficient. The residence permit must moreover already exist by 31 December of the calendar year BEFORE the course starts, i.e. before the student has arrived.
deadline_2027_intake: 2026-2027 convocatoria (Resolución de 23 de marzo de 2026, BOE-B-2026-9261): 'desde el día 7 de abril de 2026, a las 8,00, hora peninsular, hasta el día 18 de mayo de 2026, a las 15,00, hora peninsular'. The 2027-2028 convocatoria is NOT YET PUBLISHED (NOT FOUND). Note the structural trap even if the candidate somehow qualified: the window closes in MAY, months before a September enrolment, and the residence-permit cut-off is the PRECEDING 31 December.

funder: Generalitat de Catalunya - Agencia de Gestio d'Ajuts Universitaris i de Recerca (AGAUR)
amount_detail: Modular beca: exempcio/component de matricula plus quantia variable per renda i rendiment academic. Exact 2026-27 amounts not captured; the matricula-waiver component is stated to be exempt from the EU-nationality residence conditions, but NOT from the non-EU residence-permit rule.

eligibility_verbatim: Non-EU applicants: 'cal tenir permis de residencia a Espanya es a dir NIE/TIE (Targeta Identificacio Estranger). No serveix el permis d'estada per estudis.' This condition must be satisfied as at 31 December of the year preceding the call. Separately: the applicant must have 'domicili familiar a Catalunya' as at 31 December of the year preceding the call. This is the same legal distinction the Catalan pricing decree makes in Decret 96/2026 art. 1.5 ('l'autoritzacio d'estada de llarga durada per estudis ... no equival a la condicio de residents'), applied here to funding instead of fees.
deadline_2027_intake: The 2026-2027 call ran from late March to mid-May 2026 ('finals de marc a mitjan maig de 2026'), closing 18 May. The equivalent 2027-2028 window is therefore expected around March-May 2027, i.e. BEFORE the September 2027 intake - but it is irrelevant to this candidate, who cannot meet the residence condition at 31.12.2026.
notes: DOUBLE BLOCKER, either one fatal on its own: (1) non-EU applicants need a residence permit, and a study-stay permit is expressly excluded; (2) family domicile must be in Catalonia at 31 December of the preceding year. The candidate is a Tunisian non-resident with no family in Catalonia, so both fail. The brief's note that from 2026/27 AGAUR's beca general ABSORBED the state beca for Catalan-domiciled students makes this WORSE, not better: it means that for a student at a Catalan university there is now a single consolidated route, and that route carries the Catalan residence condition. name: Bonificacion del 99% del precio de los creditos superados en primera matricula (Junta de Andalucia)
funder: Junta de Andalucia - Consejeria de Universidad, Investigacion e Innovacion
amount_detail: 99% of the price of the credits the student passed at FIRST enrolment, deducted from the following year's matricula. Combined with Andalusia's low tariff (13.68 EUR/ECTS, Grupo 3 Ingenierias, non-habilitante master) this makes the second year of study effectively free. NOT income-tested - it depends on academic performance, not family means.
covers: Grado and MASTER at centros propios y adscritos of the Andalusian public universities (and Andalusian UNED associated centres where also empadronado in Andalucia).
tunisian_eligible: NO FOR THE FIRST YEAR OF A MASTER; CONDITIONAL YES FROM THE SECOND YEAR ONWARD
eligibility_verbatim: Art. 12.1 Decreto 98/2023: 'El estudiantado de los centros propios y adscritos de las universidades publicas andaluzas tendra derecho, en el curso academico de que se trate, a una bonificacion equivalente al 99% del precio de los creditos que hubiera superado en primera matricula en sus estudios de Grado y Master ... cuando se cumplan los siguientes requisitos: ... b) En la PRIMERA MATRICULACION en los estudios de Master, cuando haya estado matriculado en centros propios o adscritos de universidades publicas andaluzas o en ensenanzas artisticas superiores en centros publicos de la Comunidad Autonoma de Andalucia, DURANTE LOS DOS CURSOS ANTERIORES, en los estudios que hayan dado acceso al Master ... c) En la SEGUNDA O SUCESIVA MATRICULACION de estudios de Master, cuando haya estado matriculado en centros propios o adscritos de las universidades publicas andaluzas durante el curso anterior, tomandose en consideracion a efectos de la bonificacion, los creditos correspondientes a asignaturas superadas en primera matricula en dicho curso.'
exclusion_clause_verbatim: 'Quienes hayan sido beneficiarios de una bonificacion total o parcial en dos titulos de Master no podran obtenerla en un tercero o sucesivos.' Also, per the Junta's own guidance, the bonificacion is directed at those who do not meet the requirements for the Ministry of Education beca, accredited by declaracion responsable - a condition this candidate satisfies trivially, since wave 3 established every central-government route is closed to him.
deadline_2027_intake: No separate application window: the bonificacion is applied automatically at matricula by the university, with a declaracion responsable. It is a fee mechanism inside the precios publicos decree, not a call-based beca.
notes: THE MOST IMPORTANT POSITIVE FINDING IN THIS BLOCK, and the only regional mechanism in Spain identified as reachable by this candidate. CRITICALLY, art. 12 contains NO nationality condition and NO residence condition - the gate is purely 'were you enrolled at an Andalusian public university in the qualifying prior period'. That gate is what excludes the first year: art. 12.1.b requires prior enrolment at an Andalusian public university (or Andalusian public ensenanzas artisticas superiores) during the two preceding courses in the studies that gave access to the master, which a Tunisian arriving from SMU MedTech cannot satisfy. But art. 12.1.c opens the SECOND and subsequent enrolments to anyone enrolled in an Andalusian public university the previous course - which the candidate WILL be, from year 2 of a 90/120-ECTS master or on any repeated/carried credits. So on a two-year master in Andalusia, year 1 is charged at 13.68 EUR/ECTS with no non-EU surcharge (Andalusia's art. 3.2 leaves the surcharge to each university and Universidad de Sevilla publishes none), and year 2 attracts a 99% bonificacion on the credits passed at first enrolment in year 1. This is by a wide margin the cheapest realistic public route found in the whole sweep. ACTION FOR WAVE 4: confirm per target university (US, UGR, UMA, UCA, UPO, UJA, UAL, UHU, UCO) that (a) it publishes no extracomunitario surcharge under art. 3.2, and (b) it applies art. 12.1.c to international students without an added residence rule of its own. UJA publishes an 'incidencias con la bonificacion' page suggesting per-university administration varies.

funder: Fundación Bancaria "la Caixa" (co-funded historically by the EU H2020 Marie Skłodowska-Curie COFUND grant agreement No 713673)
amount_detail: Rules for participation §2.1: "€35,800 per year to cover the fellow's labour costs. This amount includes the Social Security cost and any other compulsory fee or compensation... as well as the fellow's annual gross salary." / "In any case, the minimum annual gross salary to be offered to the fellow by the host institution must be €25,000. If the total labour costs exceed the maximum amount offered by the ''la Caixa'' Foundation, the host institution will cover the excess." / "€3,500 per year for research costs such as conferences, courses, research stays, consumables, equipment, charges for the use of intellectual property, etc." / "The tuition fees to the official doctoral programme where the fellow will be admitted to." §1.5: "The fellowship will have a duration of up to four years." 30 fellowships per call. This is a LABOUR CONTRACT with the host institution, not a stipend: §1.3 "the host organisation will hire the fellow using the funds provided by the ''la Caixa'' Foundation."
eligibility_verbatim: §4.1 Nationality: "Young researchers of any nationality are eligible to apply for the Doctoral INPhINIT Incoming Fellowships Programme." || §4.2 Studies pursued: "Applicants must hold a higher education degree that makes them eligible to enrol in a doctoral programme before starting at their host institutions. The host university will verify, upon starting the admission process to the doctoral programme, that the studies taken up by the selected candidates make them eligible to enrol in an official doctoral programme in accordance with the regulations in force in Spain or Portugal. Should they be found not eligible after verification, the fellowship will be withdrawn. Candidates must not have been enrolled in a doctoral programme prior to the start of the fellowship." || §4.4 Research experience: "On the deadline for applications, applicants must still be within the first four years (full-time equivalent research experience) of their research careers." || §4.5 Mobility: "Candidates cannot have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of destination (Spain/Portugal) for more than twelve months in the three years immediately prior to the deadline for applications." || Call page: "30 fellowships to pursue PhD studies in research centres accredited with the Spanish Seal of Excellence Severo Ochoa, María de Maeztu or Health Institute Carlos III...", "STEM disciplines (technology, engineering, physics, chemistry, mathematics, health and life sciences)."
exclusion_clause_verbatim: §4.3 Language proficiency: "Applicants must accredit their proficiency in the English language by submitting any of the certificates mentioned below. Under no circumstances will any other certificate be accepted, despite being issued by the same organisations and/or accredit equivalence with any of the accepted levels." — the exemption list (Australia, Canada, Ireland, Malta, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa, UK, USA, Caribbean states…) does NOT include Tunisia or France, so a Tunisian applicant educated in Tunisia MUST produce one of the named English certificates. || §4.5 Mobility (operates as an exclusion once the candidate has lived in Spain): "Candidates cannot have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of destination (Spain/Portugal) for more than twelve months in the three years immediately prior to the deadline for applications." || §10.5: "Candidates must not be included on international sanctions lists, such as the United Nations, the European Union, HM Treasury and/or the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), among others."
deadline_2027_intake: The 2026 Incoming call is CLOSED: "End: 28 January 2026, at 2 pm Peninsular Spain"; shortlisting 27 April 2026, interviews 20-22 May 2026, final result 29 May 2026. The 2027 call dates are NOT YET PUBLISHED as of 2026-08-25; the pattern is an opening in autumn with a late-January deadline. Applicants can register for a notification on the fellowships application site.
notes: TIMING TRAP, AND IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN THIS RECORD. The mobility rule cuts BOTH ways for this candidate. (a) RIGHT NOW, with no prior Spanish residency, the candidate satisfies the Incoming mobility rule perfectly — this is one of the very few first-rate funded routes a Tunisian can enter directly from Tunisia. (b) BUT it funds a DOCTORATE, not a master's, so it does not pay for the September 2027 master's at all. (c) AND once the candidate has spent more than twelve months in Spain doing that master's, the Incoming call is permanently closed to them and they must switch to the Retaining call instead (separate record). So the two routes are mutually exclusive in sequence, and the choice of which one to aim at should be made deliberately, not discovered late. Second unresolved point: §4.2 requires a degree that makes you eligible to enrol in a Spanish doctoral programme, and that is judged by the host university, not by ''la Caixa''. Whether a Tunisian 5-year, 300-ECTS Software Engineering diploma on its own gives Spanish doctoral access (RD 99/2011 normally wants 300 ECTS of which at least 60 at master level) is NOT RESOLVED here and must be asked of the specific host university — this is exactly the 300-ECTS question the shared brief flags. Third: the English certificate is compulsory and the accepted list is closed — a Tunisian applicant cannot substitute a different certificate however equivalent.

name: Becas Santander / Santander Open Academy (umbrella programme — scholarships delivered per call and per partner university)
funder: Banco Santander (Santander Universidades / Santander Open Academy)
amount_detail: NO SINGLE AMOUNT — this is a catalogue, not one scholarship. Each call sets its own award. "More than 900 programmes"; "+1,000 universities, institutions and organisations collaborating in 13 countries". Most catalogue items are FREE ONLINE COURSES (language, skills, tech) worth no cash to a master's student; the cash-bearing lines are the Academic Mobility, Research, Professional Internships and Financial Assistance categories, which are published per partner university.
covers: Four declared scholarship categories: "Financial Assistance — Scholarships for financial assistance to support undergraduate studies and university access for those in need. Academic Mobility — Scholarships for national and international mobility to study at another academic institution. Research — Scholarships for students and faculty to support research in a specific program or project. Professional Internships — Scholarships to facilitate access to the job market through professional internships."
eligibility_verbatim: Platform-level: "To sign up and start learning, you just need to be over 16 years old. We believe in your potential and want to help you succeed, whether or not you're a bank customer." / "Anyone can register on Santander Open Academy — you do not need to be a Banco Santander customer." / FAQ, 'Can I access from any country?': "Yes, Santander Open Academy is globally accessible. You only need an internet connection to access it from Europe, the Americas or any other region. There are no specific residency requirements for direct-access courses. There may be geographic specifications for programmes with limited places and scholarships. Always check the Legal Terms of each programme." / "Who can apply for Santander Open Academy scholarships? The scholarships are aimed at a wide variety of profiles, from university students to professionals. Each call may have specific requirements, so review the eligibility criteria."
exclusion_clause_verbatim: There is NO nationality bar at the umbrella level — the bar is institutional affiliation. FAQ, 'What happens if my university does not appear on the list?': "Some programmes are specifically aimed at students from certain universities. If this is the case and your university is not among the participants, you will not be able to apply for that particular programme. But don't worry — you are sure to find other programmes you can participate in!" And: "Partner institution programmes — The universities and institutions we work with also publish their own programmes for their academic communities." Plus the geographic caveat: "There may be geographic specifications for programmes with limited places and scholarships."
deadline_2027_intake: NOT APPLICABLE at umbrella level — deadlines are per call, rolling throughout the year, published on app.santanderopenacademy.com. NOT FOUND for any specific Spain master's call for the Sept-2027 intake.
notes: UMBRELLA MECHANICS — the answer to 'can a non-EU applicant hold one' is YES IN PRINCIPLE, NO IN PRACTICE UNTIL ADMITTED. Nationality is not a filter: registration is open worldwide to anyone over 16, no Santander banking relationship needed, and there is no citizenship clause anywhere in the platform terms. The real gate is that money-bearing Santander scholarships are issued THROUGH a partner university to ITS OWN academic community — you must already be a student of (or admitted to) a participating institution before you can even see the call in your account, and if your university is not on the list the application form will not open. CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS CANDIDATE: a Santander scholarship is NOT an admission-stage funding route and cannot be counted on when choosing where to apply. It becomes reachable only AFTER securing a place at a Spanish partner university, and then only for whatever that university happens to publish (typically mobility grants, internship grants, or small tuition-assistance awards — rarely full master's tuition). Treat it as a possible top-up in year 1, never as the plan. ACTION FOR A HUMAN: once a target university is chosen, check that university's own Santander Universidades page for the specific call and its Legal Terms (Términos legales), which is where any nationality/residency clause would live. CAVEAT ON COVERAGE: I could not enumerate the live call catalogue — app.santanderopenacademy.com/en/program/search is a JavaScript SPA that returns only an empty shell to automated fetching, and its JS bundle is served 403, so no specific Spain-master's call could be inspected. The WebSearch budget for this session was exhausted before I could search for one. This is a genuine gap, not a finding of absence.

name: Student stay (estancia de larga duración por estudios) — right to paid work, 30 h/week, no separate work permit
funder: Gobierno de España — Reglamento de la LO 4/2000, aprobado por Real Decreto 1155/2024 (in force 20 May 2025)
amount_detail: N/A — this is the legal ceiling on paid work, not an award. Cap: 30 hours per week. Pay must comply with the applicable convenio colectivo: "siempre y cuando las condiciones laborales se ajusten a la normativa vigente y al convenio colectivo aplicable para la actividad a ejercer" (art. 57.1).
eligibility_verbatim: Art. 57.1, párrafo 4: "La autorización de estancia de larga duración obtenida en virtud de los supuestos establecidos en el artículo 52.1, letra a), autorizará a trabajar por cuenta propia y ajena, automáticamente y sin necesidad de un trámite adicional, siempre que esta actividad laboral sea compatible con la realización de esos estudios." || Art. 57.2: "Con carácter general, la actividad laboral a la que se refiere el apartado primero del presente artículo no podrá ser superior a las treinta horas semanales, salvo en el caso de la formación profesional de régimen intensivo que se estará a lo que determine la legislación sectorial. El incumplimiento de dicho límite será causa de extinción de la autorización estancia de larga duración." || Art. 52.1.a) (who this covers): "Realización de estudios superiores, como actividad principal, en una institución o centro de enseñanza superior reconocido en España, en el marco de un programa a tiempo completo, que conduzca a la obtención de un título de educación superior reconocido." || Art. 57.5: "En caso de que la persona titular de la autorización ejerza una actividad laboral en los términos previstos en este artículo, el requisito de seguro médico establecido en el artículo 35 se entenderá cumplido mediante el alta en el régimen correspondiente de la Seguridad Social." || Curricular internships need nothing extra: "No será preciso solicitar otra autorización adicional para realizar prácticas curriculares, entendiendo por tales las que formen parte del plan de estudios o formación para el que se otorgó la autorización de estancia de larga duración... Las prácticas académicas externas curriculares en entidades públicas o privadas y la fase de formación en empresa u organismo equiparado tendrán dicha consideración, y, por tanto, su realización estará cubierta por la autorización de estancia de larga duración por estudios concedida."
exclusion_clause_verbatim: Geographic limit — art. 57.3: "La autorización se limitará geográficamente a la comunidad autónoma en la que se haya concedido la autorización de estancia de larga duración. No obstante, se podrá realizar actividad laboral en localidades de otra comunidad autónoma siempre y cuando sean localidades limítrofes con la comunidad autónoma en la que se haya concedido la autorización de estancia de larga duración." || Duration tie — art. 57.4: "La vigencia de la autorización para trabajar coincidirá con la de la autorización de estancia de larga duración. La pérdida o denegación de la prórroga de la autorización de la estancia de larga duración será causa de extinción de la autorización para trabajar." || Compatibility — art. 57.1, párrafo 3: "Dichas actividades deberán ser compatibles con la realización de aquéllas para las que, con carácter principal, se concedió la autorización de estancia de larga duración."
deadline_2027_intake: N/A — standing law. In force since 2025-05-20 (RD 1155/2024 entered into force six months after BOE publication of 2024-11-20).
notes: THIS IS THE GATING FACT FOR THE WHOLE BLOCK, and the answer is favourable. A Tunisian citizen holding a Spanish student stay authorisation for a full-time official master's (art. 52.1.a) may work up to 30 h/week, employed or self-employed, AUTOMATICALLY, with NO separate work permit. This is a change from the old RD 557/2011 regime (20 h/week and an employer-initiated autorización de trabajo). Consequences: (1) a paid RA/TA contract at a lab is legally holdable; (2) part-time paid work in general is holdable; (3) the employer must register the student with the Seguridad Social, and that registration then substitutes for the private health-insurance requirement of art. 35; (4) the job must be in the same autonomous community as the study authorisation (or a bordering locality) — so a Barcelona student cannot casually hold a Madrid contract; (5) exceeding 30 h/week is an express ground for EXTINCTION of the stay authorisation — this is not a soft limit. Note also art. 52.1.a) expressly includes títulos propios within 'estudios superiores' for visa purposes, so a título propio does not by itself defeat the student visa (it still defeats PhD access and public funding — see the shared brief). Text obtained from the BOE consolidated version, fetched directly and quoted verbatim.

name: Conversion from student stay to residence-and-work authorisation after the master's (modificación art. 190 RD 1155/2024)
funder: Gobierno de España — Reglamento de la LO 4/2000 (RD 1155/2024), art. 190
amount_detail: N/A — status change, not an award. Enables a full-time salaried contract (e.g. a predoctoral contract or an industry job) after graduation without leaving Spain and without a new visa.
eligibility_verbatim: Art. 190.1: "Las personas extranjeras que se encuentren en España con una autorización de estancia de larga duración concedida para llevar a cabo los estudios o las actividades formativas previstos en los apartados a), b) y los números 4.º y 5.º del apartado e) del artículo 52 podrán acceder a la situación de residencia y trabajo y de residencia con excepción de la autorización de trabajo sin necesidad de solicitar visado, si han obtenido la titulación o el certificado correspondiente a los estudios o formación realizados y cumplen los requisitos establecidos en los apartados siguientes." || Art. 190.2: "Para obtener una autorización de residencia y trabajo por cuenta ajena será necesario cumplir los requisitos del artículo 74, excepto lo previsto en su apartado 1.a). La solicitud de la autorización podrá ser presentada tanto por el empleador como por el titular de la autorización por estudios. En todo caso, el empleador asumirá el pago de la correspondiente tasa."
exclusion_clause_verbatim: Art. 190.1, último inciso: "Además, será requisito que la persona extranjera no haya sido becada o subvencionada por organismos públicos o privados dentro de programas de cooperación para el desarrollo sostenible o de acción humanitaria españoles o del país de origen."
deadline_2027_intake: N/A — standing law, applied on completion of the master's (i.e. from mid/late 2028 for a Sept-2027 intake).
notes: MATERIAL WARNING attached to this record: the art. 190 route out of a student visa into a full work/residence permit is BLOCKED for anyone who financed the studies with a development-cooperation or humanitarian-action scholarship, whether Spanish or from the home country. That clause is directly relevant to a Tunisian candidate, because several Spanish scholarships open to Tunisians are administered under development-cooperation programmes (e.g. AECID-type instruments). Before accepting any award, check whether the awarding instrument is legally classified as 'cooperación para el desarrollo' — if it is, taking it can cost the post-study conversion route. Also note art. 190.2 removes the national-employment-situation test (art. 74.1.a), which is the single biggest practical barrier to a non-EU hire — so a graduate converting from a student visa is much easier for a Spanish lab or company to hire than a candidate applying from abroad.

amount_detail: NOT FOUND — the Students page lists what it offers in kind ("Infrastructures, guidance and means to develop your work", supervision, team) and does NOT state any stipend, grant or hourly rate. Do not assume it is paid.

The binding practical condition is the stated one: "We have agreements with different universities" — access runs through a convenio between Vicomtech and YOUR university, so a student at a university with no Vicomtech agreement has no route in.
deadline_2027_intake: No published call or deadline — placements are arranged through the university agreement and the centre's job-offers listing.
notes: GEOGRAPHIC WARNING specific to this candidate: Vicomtech is in the Basque Country. Art. 57.3 RD 1155/2024 limits a student's work authorisation to the autonomous community that granted the study authorisation (plus bordering localities). A student enrolled in Barcelona or Madrid therefore CANNOT simply take a paid Vicomtech placement in Donostia — it would need to be either a curricular internship covered by the study plan or a study authorisation granted in Euskadi. This is the single most-missed constraint on 'thesis in a company' routes and it applies to Tecnalia (Euskadi) too. Research fit is strong for path AA (Visual Computing and Interaction, Artificial Intelligence); Vicomtech also works in speech and language technologies. The 'Possible employment contract when you finish' line is the real value: it is a documented conversion path, and art. 190 RD 1155/2024 lets a graduate convert a student stay into residence-and-work without a visa and without the labour-market test.

name: TFM en empresa / prácticas académicas externas — how an industry-hosted master's thesis is (or is not) paid
funder: Legal frame: Real Decreto 592/2014, de 11 de julio, por el que se regulan las prácticas académicas externas de los estudiantes universitarios; plus Disposición adicional 52ª of the Ley General de la Seguridad Social (RDLeg 8/2015), as introduced by Real Decreto-ley 2/2023. Money, when there is any, comes from the host company.
amount_detail: THERE IS NO LEGAL MINIMUM AND NO TYPICAL AMOUNT SET BY LAW. Payment is optional and named a 'bolsa o ayuda al estudio', not a salary. RD 592/2014 art. 9.1.d) gives the student the right "A percibir, EN LOS CASOS EN QUE ASÍ SE ESTIPULE, la aportación económica de la entidad colaboradora, en concepto de bolsa o ayuda al estudio" (emphasis on the conditional). Art. 7.2.e) makes the convenio state "La existencia, en su caso, de una bolsa o ayuda de estudios para el estudiante y la forma de su satisfacción." Any figure quoted by a specific company is that company's own offer — this block records NO typical amount because none is published in law and inventing one would be a corrupted fact.
eligibility_verbatim: RD 592/2014 art. 8.1: "Podrán realizar prácticas académicas externas: a) Los estudiantes matriculados en cualquier enseñanza impartida por la Universidad o por los Centros adscritos a la misma. b) Los estudiantes de otras universidades españolas o extranjeras que, en virtud de programas de movilidad académica o de convenios establecidos entre las mismas, se encuentren cursando estudios en la Universidad..." — NO nationality condition; the condition is enrolment. || Art. 8.2: "a) Estar matriculado en la enseñanza universitaria a la que se vinculan las competencias... b) En el caso de prácticas externas curriculares, estar matriculado en la asignatura vinculada, según el Plan de Estudios de que se trate. c) No mantener ninguna relación contractual con la empresa, institución o entidad pública o privada o la propia universidad en la que se van a realizar las prácticas, salvo autorización con arreglo a la normativa interna de cada Universidad." || Immigration side, RD 1155/2024 art. 57.1: "No será preciso solicitar otra autorización adicional para realizar prácticas curriculares, entendiendo por tales las que formen parte del plan de estudios o formación para el que se otorgó la autorización de estancia de larga duración, que se produzcan en el marco de los correspondientes convenios de colaboración entre las entidades públicas o privadas y la institución de educación superior... y que no tengan carácter laboral." || Social Security, LGSS DA 52ª.1: "La realización de prácticas formativas en empresas, instituciones o entidades incluidas en programas de formación y la realización de prácticas académicas externas al amparo de la respectiva regulación legal y reglamentaria, determinará la inclusión en el sistema de la Seguridad Social de las personas que las realicen..." covering "a) Las realizadas por alumnos universitarios, tanto las dirigidas a la obtención de titulaciones oficiales de grado y máster, doctorado, como las dirigidas a la obtención de un título propio de la universidad..." DA 52ª.2: "...quedarán comprendidas como asimiladas a trabajadores por cuenta ajena en el Régimen General de la Seguridad Social..." DA 52ª.4.a): "En el caso de las prácticas formativas remuneradas, el cumplimiento de las obligaciones de Seguridad Social corresponderá a la entidad u organismo que financie el programa de formación, que asumirá a estos efectos la condición de empresario."
exclusion_clause_verbatim: RD 592/2014 art. 2.3 — the clause that defines what a TFM en empresa is NOT: "Dado el carácter formativo de las prácticas académicas externas, de su realización no se derivarán, en ningún caso, obligaciones propias de una relación laboral, ni su contenido podrá dar lugar a la sustitución de la prestación laboral propia de puestos de trabajo." || Art. 2.4: "...en el caso de que al término de los estudios el estudiante se incorporase a la plantilla de la entidad colaboradora, el tiempo de las prácticas no se computará a efectos de antigüedad ni eximirá del período de prueba..." || LGSS DA 52ª.3: "La acción protectora será la correspondiente al régimen de Seguridad Social aplicable, con la exclusión de la protección por desempleo, de la cobertura del Fondo de Garantía Salarial y por Formación Profesional. En el supuesto de las prácticas no remuneradas se excluirá también la protección por la prestación de incapacidad temporal derivada de contingencias comunes." || Duration cap on the non-curricular kind, art. 5.1.b): "Las prácticas externas extracurriculares tendrán una duración preferentemente no superior al cincuenta por ciento del curso académico..."
deadline_2027_intake: N/A — standing law. Placements are arranged inside the academic year through the university's practicas office and a convenio de cooperación educativa; there is no national call or deadline.
notes: ANSWERS THE CRITICAL QUESTION IN THREE PARTS. (1) CAN A TUNISIAN STUDENT HOLD ONE? Yes for the CURRICULAR kind, unambiguously: art. 57.1 RD 1155/2024 says in terms that no additional authorisation is needed for prácticas curriculares done under a convenio, and that they are covered by the study authorisation itself. (2) IS IT PAID? Not necessarily. The law makes payment OPTIONAL ('en los casos en que así se estipule') and calls it a bolsa or ayuda al estudio, explicitly not a wage. There is no statutory minimum. So 'TFM en empresa' is NOT a funding route you can count on — it is a route that MAY carry money, entirely at the company's discretion, and the amount must be read off the individual offer. Anyone presenting a standard figure for this is guessing. (3) THE ONE THING THAT DID CHANGE: since RD-ley 2/2023 introduced LGSS DA 52ª, ALL such placements — paid AND unpaid, official master's AND título propio — must be registered with the Seguridad Social, with the funding entity acting as employer for paid ones. That gives the student a contributory record and, for a student-visa holder, alta in the Seguridad Social also satisfies the art. 35 health-insurance requirement per art. 57.5 RD 1155/2024. UNRESOLVED POINT, FLAGGED HONESTLY: art. 57.1 names prácticas CURRICULARES only. EXTRACURRICULAR prácticas are not named in that paragraph, and they sit awkwardly between two regimes — art. 2.3 RD 592/2014 says they are not a labour relation, while the automatic authorisation in art. 57.1 para 4 is worded as authorisation 'a trabajar por cuenta propia y ajena'. Whether an extracurricular práctica needs anything extra for a non-EU student is NOT RESOLVED by the texts read here. Ask the university's international office before signing one; do not assume either answer.

name: FPU — Ayudas para la Formación de Profesorado Universitario (predoctoral contract)
funder: Ministerio de Ciencia, Innovación y Universidades; from the 2026 call processed entirely by the Agencia Estatal de Investigación (AEI)
amount_detail: AEI FPU 2026 page: "La cuantía individual total de la ayuda en la convocatoria 2026 es de 143.350€", broken down as: "Contrato predoctoral — 32.500€/año (≈130.000€ por 4 años) — Retribución salarial y cuota empresarial de la Seguridad Social. Mínimo: 75% del convenio aplicable."; "Indemnización por fin de contrato — 3.350€ — Importe total a la finalización del contrato."; "Estancias y matrícula de doctorado — 10.000€ — Estancias en centros de I+D y matrícula del programa de doctorado. Importe total para los 4 años." Note 32,500 EUR/year is the total cost to the funder including employer Social Security, not the gross salary.
eligibility_verbatim: AEI FPU 2026 page, characteristic 03 ("Sin matricularse aún para solicitar"): "Basta con estar admitido/a en un programa de doctorado, o en disposición de estarlo al firmar el contrato." || Characteristic 02 ("La solicitud la presenta el centro"): "El centro de I+D, no la persona doctoranda, es la entidad beneficiaria que firma y envía la solicitud completa." || "La FPU es una colaboración entre el/la solicitante y un centro de I+D que te contrata. Sin centro confirmado, no hay solicitud que presentar." || Characteristic 01: "Primera convocatoria FPU tramitada íntegramente por la Agencia Estatal de Investigación, con sus procedimientos." (legal basis cited on the page: RD 265/2026).
exclusion_clause_verbatim: THE MASTER'S MUST EFFECTIVELY BE DONE. The requirement is admission to a doctoral programme (or being 'en disposición de estarlo' at contract signature), and Spanish doctoral admission normally presupposes a completed master's. FPU therefore does NOT fund a master's and CANNOT be used to pay for the September 2027 master's year. No explicit nationality exclusion was found on the AEI page; the full nationality and residency conditions live in the convocatoria resolution, which was NOT fetched — treat nationality as NOT VERIFIED rather than as open.
deadline_2027_intake: FPU 2026 call (the most recent published): "Periodo de presentación: del 20 de octubre al 20 de noviembre de 2026. La persona doctoranda y el centro presentan la solicitud por vía telemática." Provisional resolution June 2027; "Octubre 2027 — Firma de contrato e incorporación". These are 2026-call dates and must NOT be shifted forward a year. For this candidate the realistic target is the FPU call of autumn 2028, after finishing a Sept-2027 master's.
notes: BE PRECISE, AS INSTRUCTED: FPU is NOT a master's scholarship and there is no version of it that funds the master's year. It is a 4-year predoctoral labour contract that begins after doctoral admission. Two structural features matter more than the money: (1) the APPLICATION IS FILED BY THE CENTRE, not the student — 'Sin centro confirmado, no hay solicitud que presentar' — so the real work is securing a supervisor and a host, which is exactly what a year as an MTG/BSC research assistant buys you; (2) the 2026 call moved to AEI management under RD 265/2026, so older third-party guidance about FPU procedure is out of date. New in 2026 and relevant to this candidate: 'Se incorpora la posibilidad de realizar las obligaciones de docencia en la etapa de máster y no únicamente de grado' — FPU holders may now teach on master's programmes, which is the closest thing Spain has to a formal TA role. Nationality conditions were NOT verified against the convocatoria text and are recorded as unverified.
